subject: Architecture
title: Curtain Walls: Skin of Glass
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Curtain Walls: Skin of Glass.

hook.text: Skyscraper walls don't hold anything up. They're just glass curtains hung on the steel skeleton.

buildup.text: Curtain wall systems are assembled from prefabricated panels — glass, aluminum frames, and sealant.

discovery.text: Modern glass can block heat while staying transparent. Low-e coatings reflect infrared light outward.

twist.text: Early curtain walls leaked badly. The John Hancock Tower in Boston dropped glass panels onto the street.

climax.text: Today's unitized curtain walls are factory-sealed and tested to withstand hurricane-force winds.

punchline.text: The walls do nothing structural. They do everything else.

quiz.question: What happened to the John Hancock Tower's curtain wall?
options: It turned opaque in cold weather
Glass panels fell off and dropped onto the street
Wind caused the entire facade to bulge outward
